# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-17 (Extended v134)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Spring Year 5—Louis Philippe's reign)**: Paris—Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district); Rue de la Verrerie (Courfeyrac's residence); Rue Plumet (Valjean's primary house); Rue de Babylone (secret passage exit); Rue de l'Homme Armé (secondary apartment); Rue de l'Ouest (secondary apartment); Faubourg Saint-Antoine; Faubourg Saint-Marceau; wine-shops (Seven Billiards, Corinthe, Richefeu's, Café Musain); schools; Boulevard de l'Hôpital; Jardin des Plantes; Luxembourg; Saint-Jacques-du-Haut-Pas church; English provincial towns. **Environmental details**: Frost silvered hedges; chalked crooked sun on forge wall; rain threatened; wind carries salt/tar scent; road ruts and puddles after thaw; light goes early; smoke lies flat; bells ring for vespers; baker's boy often late; lines at oven grow long; cart loaded with turnips creaks past well; children chase hoop shrieking; dogs bark at nothing; clouds predicted rain wrongly.

## Primary Locations
**RUE PLUMET HOUSE (Valjean's primary residence, October 1829-present)**: Single-story pavilion in deserted Rue Plumet with garden approximately one-and-a-half acres. Two ground-floor rooms, two first-floor chambers, downstairs kitchen, upstairs boudoir, attic. Behind pavilion: narrow courtyard, low building (two rooms, cellar) for concealing inhabitants. Secret-spring door masked in building communicates via long narrow paved winding corridor (hemmed by lofty walls, hidden between garden enclosures and cultivated land) to Rue de Babylone quarter-league distant with another secret-lock door. Originally built mid-last-century by Paris Parliament chief justice as mistress-house; passed through bankruptcy; remained uninhabited and furnished with old furniture; yellow illegible notice on garden wall since 1819. October 1829: Valjean (as M. Fauchelevent, independent gentleman) hired and repaired house. **Garden characteristics (Spring Year 5)**: Left uncultivated deliberately to avoid attention; left to itself over fifty years, now extraordinary and charming. In winter: thicket black, dripping, bristling; silvery snail tracks visible on cold yellow leaf carpet. All seasons: breathes melancholy, contemplation, solitude, liberty, absence of man, presence of God. Ancient padlocked gate twisted, tottering, fastened to two moss-covered pillars; forty years of dreamers gazed through bars. **Former coquettish garden transformed**: no arbors, bowling greens, tunnels, grottos remain; magnificent disheveled obscurity falls like veil; Paphos made Eden; element of repentance rendered retreat wholesome; flower-girl now offers blossom to soul; garden returned to virginity and modesty; nature filled with shade, arranged for love.

**Door on Rue de Babylone**: Box for letters/papers; receives only tax-collector notices and guard summons. Three inhabitants (Valjean, Cosette, Toussaint) receive neither papers nor letters. **Access strategy**: Neither Valjean, Cosette, nor Toussaint enter/emerge except via Rue de Babylone door. Would be difficult to guess residence in Rue Plumet unless seen through garden gate (always closed).

**VALJEAN'S OTHER APARTMENTS**: Rue de l'Homme Armé (poor appearance); Rue de l'Ouest (poor appearance). Both remote from each other and Rue Plumet. Strategy: rotate residence monthly/six-weeks, served by porters, posing as gentleman from suburbs with temporary resting-place in town.

**GORBEAU HOUSE**: 50-52 Salpêtrière district. **JONDRETTE DEN**: Abject, fetid. Furniture: straw chair, infirm table, two pallets, straw beds. Walls: leprous, seamed, charcoal sketches, moisture. Fireplace with brazier. Dormer window (four broken panes). Colored engraving "THE DREAM" (Napoleon on blue column). Wooden panel—Battle of Waterloo: sergeant rescuer (Thénardier) carrying colonel victim (Pontmercy). Rope-ladder with hooks, verdigris candlestick.

**WINE-SHOPS & MEETING PLACES**: Centers of revolutionary fermentation. Seven Billiards, Café Rue Saint-Hyacinthe, Corinthe (Rue Mondétour), Richefeu's (Barrière du Maine), Café Musain.

**OTHER LOCATIONS**: Luxembourg (least frequented walk); Saint-Jacques-du-Haut-Pas church (poor quarter, long way off); Austerlitz bridge; Père-Lachaise; Barrière du Trône; Panthéon; Val-de-Grâce; Barrière de Grenelle; La Force prison; Les Madelonettes; Salpêtrière; Petit-Picpus convent.

## Jean Valjean and Cosette: Life at Rue Plumet (October 1829-present)
**Valjean's decision**: Recognized necessity of leaving convent after five years; anguish at requiring Cosette's departure, but concluded danger insufficient to condemn her to cloister. Decided to be prudent; adopt false identity and multiple residences to avoid Javert recapture.

**Convent departure**: Demanded audience with Reverend Prioress; fabricated story of inheritance from deceased brother. Offered five thousand francs to community as indemnity for Cosette's five years free education.

**Daily life and routine**: Cosette taught housekeeping in convent, now regulates household expenditure (modest). **Every day**: Valjean puts arm through Cosette's, takes her for walk—usually Luxembourg (least frequented walk). **Every Sunday**: Takes Cosette to mass at Saint-Jacques-du-Haut-Pas (poor quarter, long way off). Valjean bestows alms largely there; poor people surround him in church. This drew Thénardier's epistle: "To the benevolent gentleman of the church of Saint-Jacques-du-Haut-Pas." Valjean fond of taking Cosette to visit poor and sick. **No stranger ever enters house**. Toussaint brings provisions; Valjean fetches water from nearby fountain on boulevard. Wood and wine stored in half-subterranean hollow lined with rock-work near Rue de Babylone, formerly chief-justice's grotto.

**Valjean's clothing and disguise**: When going out with Cosette: dressed as retired officer (as previously seen). When going out alone (generally at night): workingman's trousers and blouse; cap concealing face. Precaution and humility both. **National Guard service**: M. Fauchelevent, independent gentleman, belongs to national guard (registered in census of 1831). **Three or four times a year** dons uniform, mounts guard willingly—correct disguise mixing him with everyone yet leaving him solitary. Attained sixtieth birthday (age of legal exemption) but does not appear over fifty; no desire to escape service nor quibble with authority; possesses no civil status, concealing name, identity, age, everything. Sum of ambition: resembling any other man who paid taxes. **Ideal**: within, angel; without, bourgeois.

**Cosette (Spring Year 5)**: Left convent still almost child; little more than fourteen; at "ungrateful age." Except for eyes (beautiful), homely rather than pretty; no ungraceful feature but awkward, thin, timid and bold at once—grown-up little girl. **Education completed**: taught religion and devotion (especially), "history" (as convents teach it), geography, grammar, participles, kings of France, little music, little drawing. **In all other respects utterly ignorant**—great charm and great peril. Soul of young girl should not be left in dark; later mirages too abrupt and lively form there. Should be gently and discreetly enlightened with reflection of realities rather than harsh direct light. Useful, graciously austere half-light dissipates puerile fears, obviates falls. Only maternal instinct—admirable intuition of virgin's memories and woman's experience—knows how to create proper half-light. Cosette accustomed to enigmatical side of destiny; hardly notices father's peculiarities. Toussaint venerates Valjean, thinks everything he does right.

## Marius Pontmercy: Psychological and Financial Crisis
**Identity and background**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, twenty years old; three years estranged from grandfather. Paternal legacy: Colonel's instruction regarding Waterloo sergeant Thénardier (Magnon recognized in painting).

**The Ambush Crisis (resolved)**: Jondrette/Thénardier plotted extortion. M. Leblanc escaped: unscrewed coin piece (used as saw), cut cords, brandished red-hot chisel. **"While red-hot iron sank into smoking wound, impassive and almost august, he fixed on Thénardier his beautiful glance, in which there was no hatred, and where suffering vanished in serene majesty."** Dashed from window. Javert positioned outside; took action before Marius's signal. Thénardier woman hurled paving-stone at Javert; Javert ducked; stone struck wall. Javert bore prisoners in three hackney-coaches.

**Aftermath (April Year 4)**: Relocated to Courfeyrac at Rue de la Verrerie; paid quarterly rent, vacated hovel. Two reasons: (1) horror of wicked poor development; (2) avoid lawsuit testimony against Thénardier. Recognized M. Leblanc as Monsieur Fabre (Cosette's biological father). Cosette believed Valjean her father; became convent scholar.

**Financial crisis (Spring Year 5)**: **First time in life, borrowed five francs from Courfeyrac; now borrows hundred-sou piece (five francs).** Poverty returned; felt icy breath. Old coat becoming impossible; new coat growing old; shirts, hat, boots wearing out.

**Work situation**: Task: turning celebrated German quarrel (Gans and Savigny controversy) into French. Cannot focus: reads four lines, attempts to write one, sees star between himself and paper, abandons task.

**Psychological state**: Passion precipitated him into chimæras without object or bottom. Lost faculty of working toward fixed goal but endowed with more clear-sightedness and rectitude than ever. Judgment almost wholly disassociated from hope. Meditation turns to reproach; reflects dolefully on idleness, paralysis of soul gaining on him, night growing more dense. **No longer even sees sun.** Yet sensations reach him: laundresses beating linen, birds chattering in elm-trees. Happy, even in anguish, is he whom God gave soul worthy of love and unhappiness.

**Marius and Cosette**: She—whole thought. One sweet idea: she loved him; glance told him so; she knew his soul. Pure reveries fell on notebook: "writing to her." **Periodical five francs a double riddle**: to Courfeyrac who lent, to unknown recipient who received. Continues dreaming of "Her."

**Éponine's approach (Spring Year 5)**: Encountered Marius on riverside. **Grown poorer and prettier—double progress toward light and distress. Barefooted and in rags; holes larger, tatters more sordid than two months prior.** Inquired where he lived (jailed fortnight, released). Revealed hunted six weeks for him; Father Mabeuf directed her. Mocked hat, called him Baron Marius. Questioned residence change from Gorbeau house.

## M. Mabeuf: Decline and Hope
**Status (Spring Year 5)**: Nearly eighty years old. Health declining; old servant Mother Plutarque ill in bed (unpaid wages fifteen months). Subsists minimally: breakfast two eggs, leaves one for servant; often only meal. No longer smiles; grown morose; no longer receives visitors. Passes Marius sometimes on Boulevard de l'Hôpital; exchange only melancholy sign of head. **"Heart-breaking that two friends become chance passers-by."**

**Projects**: _Flora of Cauteretz_ no longer sells. Indigo experiments unsuccessful in Austerlitz garden (bad exposure). Pawned _Flora_ copperplates for Jardin des Plantes corner (good exposure) for indigo trials at own expense.

**Three forms of happiness**: Books, garden, indigo. **Plans**: "When I make blueing balls, I'll be rich, withdraw copperplates from pawn-shop, put _Flora_ in vogue with money and newspaper advertisements, buy copy of Pierre de Médine's _Art de Navigier_, edition 1655."

**Daily routine**: Toils all day over indigo plot; at night waters garden, reads books.

**Mysterious visitor (early Spring Year 5)**: While sitting on overturned stone post in garden at broad daylight, emerged "tall, slender girl, who drew herself up and stared boldly. Less air of human being than form blossoming from twilight." Unhooked well-chain, withdrew bucket, filled watering-pot, ran barefooted in tattered petticoat among flower-beds distributing water. **"Sound of watering-pot on leaves filled Father Mabeuf's soul with ecstasy."** As he fell asleep: "it came back to him."

## Revolutionary Fermentation (Spring Year 5)
**Enjolras as nexus**: Believed moment at hand: people taking possession of right; revolution majestically taking France. Furnace being heated. Powder train scattered across Paris.

**Network**: Combeferre (eloquence), Feuilly (enthusiasm), Courfeyrac (dash), Bahorel (smile), Jean Prouvaire (melancholy), Joly (science), Bossuet (sarcasms). Created electric spark taking fire nearly everywhere.

**Secret societies and evidence (April Year 4)**: Public cartridge-making. Arrested Pardon. Documents found: printed dialogues, song "Workmen, band together," cartridges, bullet-mould, punch, powder, lead traces. Cipher document: Q, C, D, E = quinturions, centurions, decurions, éclaireurs; date April 15, Year 4.

**Network**: Associations of Friends of People, Society of Rights of Man, Society of Action, Gallic Society, committees, societies for liberty of press, individual liberty, instruction, equal workingmen (levellers, communists), Army of Bastilles. Military: counted on fifty-second, fifth, eighth, thirty-seventh, twentieth light cavalry. Burgundy, southern towns: liberty trees planted. Network spreading like membranes.

## Javert's Outstanding Question and Prison Intelligence Operations
**After M. Leblanc's escape (April Year 4)**: M. Leblanc's identity and whereabouts mystery. **"Assassinated man who flees more suspicious than assassin."**

**Captured**: Babet, Gueulemer. Released: Éponine, Azelma (Les Madelonettes). Montparnasse preferred Éponine over gang work. Three prowlers captured late Year 4.

**Brujon operations (Late Year 4 through February Year 5)**: Released in Charlemagne courtyard. Feigned fever, inquired about ward. End February: executed three commissions (fifty sous total)—homes of three prowlers. Placed solitary month after discovery.

**Prison communication**: "Postilion"—moulded bread pallet sent rooftop courtyard-to-courtyard with notes. Babet passed note La Force to Salpêtrière. Woman transmitted to Magnon (bridging Salpêtrière and Les Madelonettes via Éponine).

**Éponine's reconnaissance (Year 5)**: Released Les Madelonettes. Magnon handed Brujon's note. Went to Rue Plumet, recognized gate and garden, observed house, spied, lurked. Brought biscuit (prison symbol) to Magnon, transmitted to Babet's mistress.

## Louis Philippe and Historical Context
**Spring Year 5**: Handsome in old age, graceful. Lacked majesty; no crown, no white hair. Mixture suited 1830. Incorruptible; carried umbrella. Policy domestic; excessive timidity displeasing. Press, tribune, conscience, speech free. **One of best princes ever on throne.** Cloud gathering—strange shade from wraths and systems. Everything hastily stifled, fermenting. Electric tension: first comer brings light. Petty revolts suppressed but bursting afresh—sign vast underlying conflagration.
